sections_inspected: The Bearers of Italian Positivism, the Traditional Intellectuals
scope_outcomes.criterion: The citing text must make an anchored substantive claim about Weber’s role in its argument, identifying what Weber is used to support, qualify, oppose, or illuminate.
scope_outcomes.basis: The full supplied article was inspected. It places Weber in the genealogy of the externalist account linking positivism to capitalist rationalization and uses a Weberian question about life-arrangement to characterize Italian positivism as teleological.
limitations: This assessment concerns only the supplied 2021 article, not the authors’ complete work or the full reception of Weber.
The article cites Weber alongside other theorists, so the evidence does not establish that Weber alone determines the externalist framework.

sections_inspected: The Bearers of Italian Positivism, pp. 831–835
scope_outcomes.criterion: A retained row must identify an argumentative act performed with a citation to Max Weber and support that act with a verbatim clause from the citing text.
scope_outcomes.basis: Two anchored passages in the article use Weber in distinct ways: as part of a genealogy of externalist accounts and as a dialogue partner whose question frames the article’s account of teleological positivism.
limitations: This outcome concerns only the supplied 2021 article, not the authors’ complete work or Weber’s entire reception.
The article’s citations to Weber are sometimes embedded in broader citation clusters, so distinctively Weberian influence cannot always be isolated.

sections_inspected: The Bearers of Italian Positivism, the Traditional Intellectuals
scope_outcomes.criterion: A passage must attribute or express a proposition concerning Max Weber’s cited position and permit classification as adopts, builds_on, qualifies, disputes, or mentions.
scope_outcomes.basis: The article explicitly attributes Weber’s account of rationalization to the externalist proposition that modern capitalist society generates positivism and explicitly presents a Weberian question as one that Italian positivists sought to answer.
limitations: This assessment concerns the supplied article and does not establish Riley’s or the coauthors’ stance across their complete work.
The article’s broader criticism of externalist theories does not by itself establish a direct dispute with Weber’s own formulation.
